TRIPOD+AI.design: Clinical prediction models (regression or machine learning / AI)

items.topic: Identify study as developing or evaluating performance of a multivariable prediction model, target population, and outcome
See TRIPOD+AI for Abstracts checklist (13 items)
Healthcare context and rationale for developing or evaluating prediction model, referencing existing models
Target population, intended use, and intended users of model
Describe any known health inequalities relevant to prediction task
Specify study objectives including whether developing, evaluating, or both
Sources of data (e.g., RCT, cohort, EHR, registry) and dates of data collection
Key study dates including start/end of accrual and end of follow-up
Study setting (e.g., primary care, hospital) and number/location of centres
Eligibility criteria for participants
Details of any treatments received and how handled in modelling
Data preparation and preprocessing steps (cleaning, normalization, image/text pipeline)
Clearly define predicted outcome, including how and when assessed
Report any actions to blind assessment of outcome to be predicted
Report any actions to address subjectivity/inter-rater variability in outcome
Describe choice of initial predictors and any predictor selection rationale
Clearly define all predictors, including how and when measured
Report any actions to blind assessment of predictors for outcome and other predictors
Explain how study size was arrived at (sample size justification / events per predictor)
Specify how missing data were handled (imputation, indicators, complete case)
Describe how data were partitioned (train/tune/test, cross-validation, external validation) avoiding leakage
Describe how predictors were handled in analysis (transformations, encoding, non-linearity)
Specify type of model, model-building steps, hyperparameter tuning, and internal validation
Specify how heterogeneity across clusters/sites/time was handled
Specify all performance measures and plots (discrimination, calibration, clinical utility)
Describe any model updating (recalibration, re-estimation, extension) if performed
Describe how predictions were calculated from the evaluated model
Describe methods used to address class imbalance and subsequent recalibration
Describe approaches used to address or evaluate model fairness across subgroups
Specify model output (probabilities, risk groups, thresholds) and rationale
Identify any differences between development and evaluation data (setting, eligibility, outcomes, predictors)
Name institutional review board/ethics committee approval and consent/waiver
Sources of funding and role of funders
Declare any conflicts of interest of authors
Indicate where study protocol can be accessed or state none prepared
Provide registration information (register name, number) or state not registered
State availability of study data and any access restrictions
State availability of analytical code and any access restrictions
Describe patient and public involvement in design, conduct, reporting, interpretation, or state none
Describe flow of participants through study including inclusions/exclusions and follow-up
Report participant characteristics (demographics, predictors, outcomes, missingness) overall and by dataset
Compare distribution of important variables between development and evaluation datasets
Specify number of participants and outcome events in each analysis
Provide full prediction model specification (formula, weights, code, API) to allow predictions and evaluation
Report model performance estimates (discrimination, calibration, utility) with 95% CIs overall and in key subgroups
Report results of any heterogeneity assessments across clusters/sites
Report results from any model updating (updated specification and performance)
Overall interpretation of results including fairness, clinical relevance, and context of prior models
Discuss study limitations (data quality, bias, sample size, generalizability)
Usability: describe how poor-quality or unavailable input data should be handled in clinical use
Usability: specify whether human-AI interaction or specific user expertise is required
Usability: specify next steps for future research and clinical implementation
